approval_reason: User approved the planning pack, then deferred packaging in favor of local source execution.
deferred_reason: Run MDS locally first; postpone unsigned executable and installer work.

excluded: External installer publication or production deployment
Managed-project source/test, Git, PR or deployment mutation

tasks.title: Approve the daily-use Windows outcome and safety boundary
acceptance_criteria: Human authority accepts the installable/relaunchable outcome and explicit exclusions.
Uninstall and packaging cannot delete or overwrite runtime project data.
risks: External publication and deployment remain outside this approval.

tasks.title: Approve packaged resource and native dependency architecture
acceptance_criteria: The ADR names packaging target, ASAR/native-module behavior, resource roots and data ownership.
Development and packaged execution use explicit resource contracts without weakening Electron security.
risks: Native ABI or missing packaged resource can prevent launch.

tasks.title: Approve the Daily-Usable Desktop executable task graph
acceptance_criteria: Human PM/project authority approves effort, acceptance criteria and blocking edges.
Board validation reports no missing links, blocked chain or cycles.

tasks.title: Launch one unpacked Windows app with production resources
acceptance_criteria: The unpacked executable launches with renderer, preload, native SQLite and required MDS resources present.
The package excludes repository-only tests, plans, backups, settings and secrets.
risks: Packager/native binary download or ABI rebuild may require network access.

tasks.title: Prove first launch and relaunch preserve the user workspace
acceptance_criteria: An isolated packaged first launch creates a valid runtime workspace and passes bridge/workbench/evidence/graph checks.
A second launch reuses the data root and preserves sentinel/project hashes byte-for-byte; both launches exit cleanly.
risks: Windows process cleanup and file-lock timing can make packaged smoke flaky.

tasks.title: Produce an auditable unsigned NSIS installer candidate
acceptance_criteria: Packaging produces a Windows x64 NSIS installer with recorded SHA-256 and size.
The artifact is explicitly labeled unsigned and is not installed, published or deployed automatically.
risks: Unsigned installer can trigger SmartScreen and is not suitable for public distribution.

tasks.title: Produce fresh Daily-Usable Desktop Definition of Done evidence
acceptance_criteria: Fresh source and packaged verification, data preservation, content audit, artifact hashes and residual risks are recorded.
The milestone stops at the human local release gate and does not authorize publication or deployment.
risks: Manual installed-app/uninstaller behavior remains unverified until separately authorized and executed.
